title: Rapid Resistance Testing Protocol for Detection of Resistance in Enterobacteriaceae
author: Manal Tadros
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uz9ex96
materials: Preparation of bacteria and antibiotic mixture for testing:
3- LC separation and MS/MS analysis 3.3 min.
4-	Integration and quantitation of antibiotics 10 min.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Suspension
steps.instruction: Suspend a fresh (18-24 hours old), pure colony of each isolate in 2 milliliters of Mueller-Hinton broth using a sterile 1µl loop to achieve concentrations of 0.5 to 1.0 McFarland.

steps.title: Add Antibiotics and Internal Standard
steps.instruction: Add ampicillin, cefazolin, cefotaxime, and imipenem to the Mueller-Hinton broth suspension and include the internal standard oxazepam.

substeps.instruction: Add each antibiotic at an individual concentration of 0.5 µg/ml.
Add oxazepam to a final concentration of 40 ng/ml.

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Incubate the bacterial suspension with the antibiotic mixture for one hour at 37˚C in a shaking incubator with gentle agitation at 200 cycles per minute.

steps.title: Extract Antibiotics
steps.instruction: Extract the antibiotic mixture from the bacterial suspension using methanol and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 300 µl of the suspension into an Eppendorf tube.
Add 600 µl of absolute methanol.
Briefly vortex the mixture.
Centrifuge at 35,000x g in a mini-centrifuge for five minutes to remove precipitated protein.

steps.title: Prepare Sample for Injection
steps.instruction: Prepare the supernatant for LC-MS/MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 600 µl of the supernatant into a 2 ml glass injection vial.
Mix with 300 microliters of distilled LC grade water.

steps.title: Perform Chromatographic Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the mixture using a Shimadzu LC20 system with a Phenomenex C-8 column (50mm x 4.6 mm).

substeps.instruction: Set Solvent A to 5mM ammonium bicarbonate buffer (pH 7.0) and Solvent B to methanol.
Maintain flow rate at 1 ml/min.
Start with 98% solution A and 2% solution B.
Apply linear gradients: 0-0.4 min (65% B), 0.4-1.3 min (82% B), 1.3-1.4 min (98% B).
Hold flow at 98% B from 1.4-2.3 min.
Step flow to 2% B from 2.3-3.3 min.

steps.title: Perform Tandem Mass Spectrometry
steps.instruction: Analyze the separated mixture using a Sciex 3200 Qtrap mass spectrometer with a TurboIonSpray® source in positive electrospray ionization mode.

substeps.instruction: Use Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM) to quantify hydrolysis.
Select parent ions in the first quadrupole (Q1) based on mono isotopic protonated mass.
Perform collision-fragmentation in the second quadrupole (Q2).
Filter specific daughter ions in the third quadrupole.

steps.title: Quantify Antibiotic Hydrolysis
steps.instruction: Calculate the percent hydrolysis of the antibiotics using a standard curve and the internal standard.

substeps.instruction: Generate a standard curve using 4 standards: blank (0 µg/ml), Standard 1 (0.25 µg/ml), Standard 2 (0.5 µg/ml), and Standard 3 (1 µg/ml) for each of the four antibiotics.
Ensure calibration standards are incubated in the same medium under identical conditions without bacteria.

Calculate percent hydrolysis as the ratio between the recovered drug from the bacterial suspension and the parent drug concentration from the standard plot, using the oxazepam ratio for accurate quantitation.
